title: Minimize routing impedance: extract policy orchestra and localize fallback sanitation
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Overview: The smart routing layer has accrued several ad-hoc shims for policy evaluation and regional fallback sanitation. This ticket extracts the policy orchestration code into a testable, pluggable 'policy-orchestra' worker set, and relocates fallback sanitation logic from the global routing hotpath into a localized event-driven sanitizer. Goals are to reduce lock contention, lower median routing latency under burst, and make fallback transitions auditable and reversible.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluation is served by a new policy-orchestra component behind a clear RPC contract and feature flag
Global routing hotpath no longer holds the policy mutex for >2ms on P50 under synthetic burst (measured on perf harness)
Fallback sanitation is handled asynchronously with retries and idempotency; no routing request blocks on sanitation in steady-state
End-to-end canary traffic (10k requests/min) shows <=5% increase in tail latency during rollout and QoS meets existing SLOs
All new behavior covered by unit and integration tests; migration has a documented rollback plan
technical_notes: Introduce policy-orchestra: a small gRPC-backed pool of workers performing policy evaluation and enriched traces
Replace global policy mutex with optimistic cache + lease-per-key for policy results; fall back to orchestra when cache miss
Move fallback sanitation into an evented worker with scoped circuit wrappers and a bounded retry queue
Add tracing hooks to annotate fallback transitions with origin (region, capacity-tier, circuit-state) for postmortems
Plan for gradual rollout via feature-flagged canary and automatic rollback if error-rate delta > 0.5% over baseline
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Spike complete. Benchmarked mutex hold times on routing hotpath — observed P50=1.8ms, P95=7.2ms during synthetic Poisson burst
2026-03-08: Design review with Product and SRE. Agreed to use gRPC pool and keep an in-process fallback queue for single-region small tenants
2026-03-10: Initial implementation of policy-orchestra skeleton merged to feature branch. Added unit tests for lease-per-key logic (PR #8571)
2026-03-12: Integration harness run against staging shows 18% reduction in lock contention events; however tail latency increased by 3% for short-lived flows — investigating batching thresholds
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Verma): Ensure runbook includes steps to pin traffic to runtime-1.23 if rollback required
SRE (Ryan O'Connor): Add flood protection to orchestra worker queue and metrics for queue-saturation before canary
Design (Maya Patel): Prefer non-blocking fallbacks for UI routing to avoid client timeouts; will validate UX in console QA
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Orchestra becomes a new single-point-of-failure. Mitigation: multi-zone pool, circuit-breaker, and benign fallback to legacy sync path on overload
Risk: Increased number of RPC hops may add tail latency. Mitigation: local caching with short TTL and batching policy evals for identical requests
Risk: Migration reveals hidden assumptions in legacy sanitizer. Mitigation: run extended integration tests with historical traffic replay and add strict assertions for invariants
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag to route policy evals to legacy path
Drain orchestra workers and flush retry queues before disabling feature
If rollback fails, revert runtime binary to runtime-1.23 stable build and disable new config at infra layer
notes_for_release: Feature gated behind policy-orchestra FF. Default off for public tenants. Rollout plan in Confluence with step-down thresholds and SLO gates.
qa_checklist: Run historical traffic replay against staging for 24h
Canary 1% traffic for 2h; verify telemetry and error budgets
Canary 10% traffic for 4h; validate UX for console rollouts
Post-deploy smoke checks: routing traces, queue sizes, error rates
